extracted.intended_audience: AoPS community members and math students writing Asymptote diagrams (AoPS Wiki, AoPS forums, or LaTeX)
extracted.subtask_description: A basic how-to for writing Asymptote vector-graphics code and embedding it on AoPS/Wiki/LaTeX, covering syntax, comments, variable declarations, units, and output sizing. Intended to teach correct code form and practical style choices for readable diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Command termination with semicolon
rubrics_metrics.description: Each command in Asymptote must be separated by a semicolon (;). This is the convention that tells Asymptote where each command ends.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commands do not necessarily need to be on separate lines, since semicolons are the only method by which Asymptote interprets new commands. However, putting the commands on separate lines is often useful to organize your code and improve readability for people looking to interpret your code. Whitespaces before and after commands are not read, so any line can be indented freely. Example: draw((50,0)--(50,50));draw((50,0)--(0,0));

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment syntax
rubrics_metrics.description: Use '//' to start a single-line comment and '/*' ... '*/' to delimit multi-line comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Comments are lines not interpreted by Asymptote. Examples: // This is a program  and /* This is a program
that draws a triangle */. Use comments to explain code and increase readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Platform-specific embedding tags
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the correct tag/environment for embedding Asymptote depending on platform: AoPS posts use [asy]...[/asy], AoPS Wiki uses <asy>...</asy>, and LaTeX uses \begin{asy}...\end{asy}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare Asymptote code with the appropriate container so the platform recognizes and renders it. On AoPS community posts use the [asy] tag; on the AoPS Wiki use HTML-like <asy> tags; when using the Asymptote package in LaTeX use \begin{asy} and \end{asy}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variable declaration and assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Every new variable must be declared with a data type using the syntax: [datatype] [variable]; and values are assigned with '='.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can separate declaration and assignment (int n; n=3;) or combine them (int n=3;). Multiple variables can be declared at once: int m,n,d; and mixed declarations/assignments are allowed: int a,b=2,c,d=5; Use correct type names and consistent declarations to avoid type errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose appropriate data types
rubrics_metrics.description: Store data in suitable Asymptote data types (examples include real, pair, int).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tutorial mentions real numbers (real) and pairs of numbers (pair) as common types. Use real for floating values, pair for coordinate points, and int for integers. (A table of common types is referenced on the page.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate representation and origin placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Points are represented as pairs (x,y); Asymptote places your image in the center of the output page after it is drawn, so the placement of origin is usually irrelevant for final placement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the picture is centered when output, you can choose coordinate placement conveniently; nevertheless, think in (x,y) pairs when building geometry. Example: draw((0,0)--(50,50));

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand and set units (unitsize)
rubrics_metrics.description: The default unit length is the PostScript bigpoint (pt = 1/72.27 inches). Use unitsize(...) to specify the unit length for the picture; it accepts up to three arguments (picture, x unit, y unit). If only one real argument is given, both x and y unit sizes are set to that number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can set units via numeric values or unit constants, e.g. unitsize(72); sets unit to 1 inch, and unitsize(1inch); does the same. Be careful when redefining unitsize: distances between coordinate points change accordingly (e.g., points (0,0) and (1,0) are one unit apart under the current unitsize). Built-in constants include pt, inch, cm, and mm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control output dimensions with size(...)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use size(...) to specify the exact width and height of the box that your picture will be fit into. If only one number is given, both width and height are set to that number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: size scales the final rendered diagram to fit the specified box regardless of unitsize. Examples: size(5cm,5cm); or size(5cm); will fit the diagram to a 5cm x 5cm box. Use size if you need fixed output dimensions (e.g., for inclusion in documents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiment to see effects of unitsize
rubrics_metrics.description: Try sample code altering unitsize to observe how scaling changes the diagram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example exercise from the page: make an Asymptote document with unitsize(2inch); draw(unitsquare); and see what happens as you change the inch size to several other values. This is practical advice to internalize how unitsize affects rendered distances.
